issues.t: Shifter can reach Park while still in gear
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the car is not truly held in Park, so it may creep or roll after you get out.
issues.why: On some cars built in this period the shift cable was fitted incorrectly at the factory, so the lever position and the transmission's actual gear do not match. Kia recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Use the parking brake every time you park and have a Kia dealer check your VIN for the shift cable recall right away.

issues.t: Brake lights may stop working
issues.sym: Brake lights do not come on when you press the pedal, cruise control may not cancel with the brake, and a warning light may appear.
issues.why: The switch at the top of the brake pedal can fail internally, so the car no longer knows the pedal is pressed. Kia recalled affected cars to replace the switch.
issues.next: Have someone check that your brake lights work. If they do not, get the recall repair done before driving more than you must.

issues.t: Theta II engine bearing wear, knocking and seizure
issues.sym: A knock or tick that gets faster with engine speed, low oil level between changes, an oil pressure light, power loss, stalling, or the engine locking up.
issues.why: Metal debris left from machining at the engine plant can wear the connecting rod bearings until they fail. Kia recalled 2011-2014 cars, added knock-detection software, and extended engine coverage after a class action.
issues.next: Stop driving if you hear knocking or lose power, and have it towed. Check your VIN for the engine recall and any extended engine warranty, and keep oil change records.

issues.t: Fuel leak after an engine replacement
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell or fuel dripping in the engine bay, usually on a car that has had its engine replaced.
issues.why: The high-pressure fuel pipe could be damaged or not lined up correctly when a replacement engine was installed, letting fuel escape near hot parts. Kia recalled cars that had engine replacements.
issues.next: Do not drive if you smell fuel. Have the car towed to a Kia dealer and check your VIN for the fuel pipe recall.

issues.t: Airbags may not deploy in a crash
issues.sym: Usually no warning; sometimes an airbag light.
issues.why: The airbag control unit can short out during a crash, which can stop the front airbags and seat belt pretensioners from firing. Kia recalled affected cars, including hybrids.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the airbag control unit recall and have it done as soon as possible.

issues.t: ABS unit can short and catch fire
issues.sym: ABS warning light, a burning smell, or smoke from the engine bay, even when the car is parked and off.
issues.why: Brake fluid can seep into the ABS control unit and cause an electrical short. Kia ran several recalls, adding a new fuse and inspecting the unit, and told owners to park outside until repaired.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Park outdoors away from buildings and check your VIN for the ABS recalls. If you smell burning or see smoke, do not drive the car.

issues.t: Headliner trim can come loose when side airbags fire
issues.sym: Usually nothing you would notice in normal driving.
issues.why: Plates holding the headliner may not be properly secured, so they can break free when the side curtain airbags deploy and could hurt someone. Kia recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the headliner recall and schedule the free repair.

issues.t: Right front axle shaft can crack and break
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from the front right when accelerating, then a sudden loss of drive to the wheels.
issues.why: The right front driveshaft on some cars built in late 2015 and early 2016 may crack and separate. Kia recalled affected cars.
issues.next: If you hear new clunking or the car stops moving under power, pull over safely and have it towed. Check your VIN for the axle recall.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not inflate fully
issues.sym: No warning to the driver.
issues.why: On some early 2016 cars the driver's airbag was missing a chemical needed for its second inflation stage, so it may not protect as intended. Kia recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the driver airbag recall and get it repaired promptly.

issues.t: Trunk cannot be opened from inside
issues.sym: The glow-in-the-dark trunk release inside the trunk does not open the lid.
issues.why: The base of the trunk latch can crack, so the inside emergency release no longer works. Kia recalled affected cars, including hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the trunk latch recall and have the latch replaced.

issues.t: Hybrid can lose power in electric mode
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive power while running on electric power, often with warning lights.
issues.why: A voltage protection device in the hybrid system can trip when it should not, cutting power while driving. Kia recalled affected hybrids for a fix.
issues.next: If power cuts out, steer to a safe spot. Check your VIN for the hybrid power recall and avoid relying on the car until it is fixed.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking may not stop for parked cars
issues.sym: The forward collision system does not brake or warn when approaching a stopped vehicle ahead.
issues.why: A software error could keep the collision-avoidance system from applying the brakes when it detects a stationary car. Kia recalled affected cars for a software update.
issues.next: Do not depend on automatic braking. Check your VIN for the forward collision software recall.
issues.sevReason: Driver-assist limit: automatic emergency braking may not react to parked cars; the normal brakes work.

issues.t: Fuel tank can swell, melt and leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, a check-engine light, or fuel dripping under the car near the exhaust.
issues.why: A worn check valve in the fuel vapor purge system can let pressurized air from the engine into the fuel tank. The tank bulges until it touches the hot exhaust and melts. Kia recalled affected K5s.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Do not drive if you smell fuel or see a leak. Check your VIN for the purge valve recall so the valves and any damaged tank are replaced.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor fault can stall the V6
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or idling, may not restart right away, and a check engine light can come on.
issues.why: The sensor that tells the computer where the crankshaft is was built with a casing that was out of spec. A part on its circuit board can crack, and the engine loses its timing signal. Kia recalled these V6 cars to replace the sensor.
issues.next: A stall in traffic is a safety risk. Check your VIN for this recall and have the sensor replaced before relying on the car.

issues.t: Front subframe can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, steering that pulls or feels loose, or heavy flaking rust on the steel cradle under the engine, mostly on cars driven on salted winter roads.
issues.why: Road salt and water can collect inside the front subframe and rust it from within. If the metal gets weak enough, a suspension arm can pull away from it. Kia issued a recall for this.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have a shop look at the subframe on a lift soon. Do not keep driving if the front end clunks or the steering changes suddenly.

issues.t: Side airbag wiring can be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on, or there is no warning at all until a crash.
issues.why: The wiring for the seat-mounted side airbag can get damaged, which can keep that airbag from firing in a side impact. Kia recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and have any airbag light diagnosed right away, since the airbags may not protect you.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may be installed wrong (K5 recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you can see or feel. The problem only shows up when the curtain airbag does not open the way it should in a crash.
issues.why: On some K5 sedans the side curtain airbags may not have been fitted correctly at the factory, so they might not unfold properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and book the free inspection soon. The dealer refits the airbags if needed.

issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission can lose drive (K5 GT recall)
issues.sym: Transmission warning messages, then the car stops pulling and coasts, sometimes within seconds of the warning.
issues.why: The oil pump inside the 8-speed dual-clutch transmission can fail. The backup limp mode that should let you keep moving may not work, so drive power is lost.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If a transmission warning appears, pull over somewhere safe and have the car towed to a Kia dealer.

issues.t: Steering can turn heavy with lane following on (K5 GT recall)
issues.sym: With Lane Following Assist on in a curve, the steering wheel suddenly takes more effort to turn.
issues.why: The power steering software may miss a communication fault, so the steering assist does not adjust as it should while the lane system is steering.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the power steering software recall and keep both hands on the wheel when using lane following until it is done.

issues.t: Rear window trim can come loose and fly off (K5 recall)
issues.sym: The glossy trim piece beside the rear side window looks lifted, rattles or whistles at speed, or is missing.
issues.why: The trim on the rear roof pillar may not be held on well enough and can work loose. A piece that comes off on the road is a hazard to other drivers.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and press on both trim pieces now and then. If one is loose, tape it down and have the dealer replace it.

issues.t: Parking lights can flicker (K5 recall)
issues.sym: The parking lights flicker or pulse instead of staying steadily lit.
issues.why: A software error in the module that manages electrical power can make the parking lights flicker, which makes the car harder for others to see.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall and get the free software update, at the dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (K5 recall)
issues.sym: The screen behind the steering wheel goes dark, so the speedometer, tire pressure reading and warning lights are not shown.
issues.why: A software error can make the instrument panel display fail while the car otherwise runs normally.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for this recall and get the free software update.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve may not seal in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing is usually noticed in normal driving. A fuel smell or damp patch under the back of the car can be a sign.
issues.why: A valve on top of the fuel tank may not close all the way, so if the car ends up on its side or roof, gasoline can spill out near hot exhaust parts or other ignition sources.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the fuel tank valve recall and have the valve replaced. If you smell raw fuel, stop driving the car and have it looked at right away.

issues.t: Clock spring wiring can disable the driver airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light on the dash, and sometimes horn or steering wheel buttons that stop working.
issues.why: The coiled wiring behind the steering wheel that feeds the driver airbag can build up high electrical resistance. The airbag computer then cannot fire the driver airbag in a crash.
issues.next: Do not ignore an airbag light. Check the VIN for the clock spring recall and have it replaced before you rely on the car.

issues.t: Low-pressure fuel hose can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell, damp fuel on the engine or a drip under the front of the car, sometimes with a rough idle.
issues.why: The rubber hose that carries fuel to the high-pressure pump sits close to engine heat. Without its heat shielding it can harden and crack, and leaking fuel in a hot engine bay is a fire risk. Kia recalled these cars twice, once for the hose and again for cars where the first repair was not done correctly.
issues.next: Do not drive the car if you smell fuel; have it towed. Check the VIN for both fuel hose recalls, since some cars needed a second visit.

issues.t: Driver's door can stop unlatching
issues.sym: The driver's door will not open from the outside handle, the inside handle, or either one, and the lock may not release with the key or the remote, so you end up climbing in from the passenger side.
issues.why: The latch and the lock actuator buried in the door wear out and jam, and the rods that link the two handles to the latch can slip or bind. Owner reports cluster well past the warranty period.
issues.next: Have the latch and lock actuator in that door replaced before the door sticks shut for good, since a door that will not open is also a problem if you ever need to get out in a hurry.

issues.t: Both low beam headlights can stop working
issues.sym: One low beam goes out, then the other follows, often not long after a new bulb was fitted, leaving almost no light on the road ahead at night.
issues.why: Owners report the bulbs and headlight units failing again and again rather than simply reaching the end of their life, which points at the lamp assemblies and their wiring. The pattern across Kia models has drawn a lawsuit investigation.
issues.next: Fit new bulbs, and if they fail again have the headlight assemblies, sockets and wiring checked instead of just buying more bulbs. Do not drive after dark with no low beams.

issues.t: Engine can use up its oil between changes
issues.sym: The dipstick reads low or empty well before the next service, the oil light may blink in corners or at idle, and the engine can start to tick or knock.
issues.why: The direct-injection Theta II four burns oil past its piston rings. Federal investigators have tied the same engine family to connecting rod bearings worn by oil starvation, which is how a quiet oil-burner turns into a seized engine.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fuel stop and top it up, keep the receipts, and ask a Kia dealer whether your VIN qualifies for extended engine coverage or the knock sensor software update. Stop driving and have it towed if it knocks.

issues.t: Flashing check engine light, code P1326 and limp mode (2020)
issues.sym: The check engine light starts flashing at highway speed, the car drops into a reduced-power mode and will not rev much past 2,000 rpm, and a code reader shows P1326. Many owners also notice a ticking or knocking sound and oil disappearing between changes.
issues.why: P1326 is set by Kia’s knock sensor detection software, which watches for the vibration of a connecting rod bearing starting to wear and then cuts power to protect the engine. Owners of 2020 cars report the same pattern seen on the recalled 2011-2019 engines, sometimes ending in an engine replacement.
issues.next: Slow down, get off the highway and avoid hard acceleration. Check the oil level right away, and have a Kia dealer inspect the engine rather than just clearing the code or swapping the knock sensor. If it knocks loudly or the oil light comes on, stop and have it towed. Keep your oil-change receipts and ask Kia in writing about warranty or goodwill coverage.

issues.t: Timing belt can snap and wreck the engine
issues.sym: The engine suddenly dies while driving and then cranks but will not start again. On high-mileage cars this often happens with no warning at all.
issues.why: These engines turn the camshafts with a rubber timing belt, and the pistons and valves share the same space. If an old belt breaks, the pistons hit the valves and bend them. Kia released an improved replacement belt for the Optima in 2005.
issues.next: If your records don't show a timing belt change at the interval in your owner's manual, have the belt, tensioner and idlers replaced soon. If the belt has already broken, stop cranking the engine and have a shop test compression to see whether the valves are bent before choosing between a head repair and a replacement engine.

issues.t: Throttle position sensor fault causes rough idle and stalling
issues.sym: Rough idle at stoplights, hesitation when you press the gas, the engine stalling, and a check engine light, sometimes with codes P0123 or P2135.
issues.why: The throttle position sensor tells the engine computer how far the throttle is open. When it sends bad readings, the computer cannot set the right idle or fuel mix. Kia issued bulletins that call for a new sensor and, in some cases, an engine computer update.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If they point to the throttle position sensor, replace it and ask the shop whether Kia's computer update applies to your car. If the engine stalls in traffic, get it fixed before relying on the car.

issues.t: Airbag light from a failed passenger seat sensor mat
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on after the engine starts, or never lights up at all during startup. Some cars fail state inspection because of it.
issues.why: A sensor mat inside the front passenger seat cushion tells the airbag computer who is sitting there. When the mat fails, the system turns on the warning light and may not switch off the passenger airbag for a child or small adult.
issues.next: Kia extended the warranty on this sensor mat to 15 years with unlimited miles for all 2006-2010 Optimas. Ask a Kia dealer to check the airbag system, which Kia says may be covered under the extension. If you already paid for this repair, ask Kia about reimbursement. Until it is fixed, keep children in the back seat.

issues.t: Hard downshift or jerk when slowing to a stop
issues.sym: The car lurches or jolts at about 20-25 mph while you brake or coast, as the automatic drops into a lower gear. Some owners say it feels like being rear-ended, and that it is worse when the engine is cold.
issues.why: The automatic transmission learns how hard to apply each clutch. When those learned values drift, downshifts become harsh. Kia has a procedure to reset the learned values and has updated the shift software, though some owners still ended up needing a transmission.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked, then ask for a software check and a reset of the transmission's learned values before agreeing to a rebuild. If the car also hesitates to accelerate after a stop, have it looked at soon, because that can be dangerous in traffic.

issues.t: Shudder or jerky launches from the dual-clutch transmission (K5 GT)
issues.sym: Shaking or shudder when pulling away from a stop, and jerky or uneven shifts at low speed.
issues.why: The K5 GT uses an 8-speed wet dual-clutch transmission. Kia issued bulletins for a judder check that can lead to clutch replacement, and software updates (SA502, later SA526) to improve how the clutches engage. This is separate from the loss-of-drive recall.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to check for the judder bulletin, the transmission software updates and recall 22V-760 on your VIN. The powertrain warranty may cover a clutch replacement. If the car ever loses drive completely, pull over safely and have it towed.

issues.t: Touchscreen freezes or radio stops responding
issues.sym: The radio will not respond to the screen or buttons, the screen freezes or maps lag with wired Apple CarPlay, or the phone connection drops.
issues.why: Software faults in the K5's infotainment unit. Kia released several software updates for an unresponsive radio, screen freezing with wired CarPlay and Bluetooth memory problems.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer to install the latest infotainment software, which is normally done under warranty. Turn off the car and open and close the driver's door to let the system fully shut down, which can clear a freeze until the update is done.

issues.t: Rough or hesitant shifts from the 8-speed automatic (2025)
issues.sym: Shifts feel rough, or the car hesitates while changing gears as you accelerate.
issues.why: The transmission's shift software on some 2025 K5s built between February 2024 and April 2025 was not tuned well. Kia released a software update (SA630) to improve shift response, also sent over the air.
issues.next: Ask a Kia dealer whether the transmission update is open on your VIN; it may be covered under warranty. If you have Kia Connect, check for an over-the-air update.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P2B59 (coolant flow valve)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on while driving, with code P2B59F0 stored. The car otherwise drives normally.
issues.why: The engine computer's logic for checking the coolant flow control valve circuit can set this code by mistake on some 2.5L engines built in 2024. Kia's fix is an engine computer update.
issues.next: Have the code read. If it is P2B59F0, ask a Kia dealer for the engine computer update in bulletin ENG264. Still check the coolant level, and if the temperature gauge climbs, pull over and stop the engine.

issues.t: Low oil level warning even when the oil is full (2026)
issues.sym: A low engine oil message appears on the dashboard now and then, even though the dipstick shows the oil level is fine.
issues.why: The engine computer misreads the oil level sensor on some 2026 K5s with the 2.5L engine built from December 2025 to March 2026. Kia released a software fix (SA642).
issues.next: Always check the dipstick first and add oil if it really is low. If the level is correct, ask a Kia dealer for the engine computer update, which may also arrive over the air with Kia Connect. If an oil pressure warning comes on, stop the engine.

issues.t: Tire sidewall bulges or blowouts on newer K5s
issues.sym: A bubble or bulge on the side of a tire, a new vibration, or a tire that fails suddenly, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.why: K5 owners have filed several complaints with NHTSA about sidewall bulges and tire failures, including on the 18-inch tires. No common cause or recall has been confirmed. A bulge means the cords inside the tire are damaged, often from a pothole or curb, but sometimes from a defect.
issues.next: A bulging tire can blow out, so put on the spare or replace the tire before driving far. Ask the tire maker's dealer about a warranty claim, and report it to NHTSA if there was no impact.
